statements.status_notes: netty 4.1.135.Final is bundled inside Google's prebuilt Java emulators (Pub/Sub, Firestore, Datastore), repackaged here unmodified. CVE-2026-59921 is a CRLF-injection issue requiring adversary-influenced header values. The emulators are local development and testing tools intended to receive traffic only from the developer's own test clients (the image documentation binds published ports to loopback); they hold no production data, so the vulnerable path cannot be exercised by an adversary in their intended use.

netty 4.1.135.Final is bundled inside Google's prebuilt Java emulators (Pub/Sub, Firestore, Datastore), repackaged here unmodified. CVE-2026-59898 is an HTTP request-smuggling issue that requires an adversary routing crafted requests through a proxy chain in front of the server; the emulators are direct-connection local endpoints with no fronting proxy in their intended use. The emulators are local development and testing tools intended to receive traffic only from the developer's own test clients (the image documentation binds published ports to loopback); they hold no production data, so the vulnerable path cannot be exercised by an adversary in their intended use.

CVE-2026-56746 is an improper-access-control issue only reachable via crafted HTTP requests from an adversary. The emulators are local development and testing tools intended to receive traffic only from the developer's own test clients (the image documentation binds published ports to loopback); they hold no production data, so the vulnerable path cannot be exercised by an adversary in their intended use.

Netty 4.1.136.Final cannot be adopted on Elasticsearch 9.4: jar-swap A/B under FIPS shows HTTPS hangs after a successful TLS handshake (TestFipsEnd2End fails creating an index). Bisect isolated the failure to netty-handler FlowControlHandler changes in 4.1.136 when loaded via the x-pack-security module, which embeds its own Netty jars and a copy of transport-netty4. Elasticsearch 9.4's HTTP pipeline uses FlowControlHandler with auto-read disabled; 8.19 does not and accepts 4.1.136.Final. Keep 9.4 on 4.1.135.Final until an upstream Elasticsearch or Netty fix lands.
